title: Inconsistent hourly usage aggregation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private causing billing spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported sudden unexplained billing spikes during hourly billing runs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The spikes are limited to specific hours and appear to correlate with usage rollups aggregated by the metering pipeline. This ticket tracks triage, a short-term mitigation, the root cause investigation, and the permanent fix.

Symptoms observed:
- Discrepancies between raw token logs and aggregated hourly usage (aggregates are sometimes 10x higher for affected hours).
- Spikes occur in all deployment modes but different trigger patterns: Hosted shows spikes tied to multi-tenant aggregation window, Dedicated shows spikes when autoscaler scales down a worker pool, Private customer reports align with nightly backup windows.
- Billing reconciliation alert triggered from Finance on 2026-03-08; 3 customers escalated to SEs and CSMs.

Initial hypothesis: A race condition in the hourly aggregator (metering-aggregator service) where late-arriving event batches overlapping aggregation boundaries are double-counted when persistence and checkpointing interleave during worker restarts or autoscale events. Additionally, a TTL-based cache eviction in the Private deployment pipeline may cause replay of deduplicated events leading to over-counting.

Scope / Impact:
- Confirmed affected customers: Acme Analytics (hosted), Nimbus Payments (dedicated), and two Private customers (internal codenames: PHOENIX, ORION). Estimated accounting delta ranges from +2% to +900% for the affected hours.
- Downstream: invoicing reports, customer dashboards, alerting and quota enforcement may be impacted.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Simulate batched ingestion with overlapping time windows and force aggregator restart during flush.
2) Re-run hourly rollup and compare raw event store (s3/gcs) token counts vs aggregated DB entries (timescaledb).
3) Validate dedupe keys for event batches; intentionally replay batches to verify counter behavior.

Short-term mitigation implemented (done):
- Snapshot freeze: temporarily paused automatic hourly billing rollups for the 2026-03-08..2026-03-10 window and triggered manual, audited reconciliation runs.
- Hotfix deployed to hosted metering-aggregator: added a conservative lock around aggregation window finalization to prevent concurrent flushes. Deployed 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3129).
- Notified impacted customers with temporary credits and initiated manual invoice corrections where required.

Work in progress (this ticket):
- Root Cause Analysis: continue detailed trace correlation between ingestion producer offsets, aggregator checkpoints, and the token accounting ledger. Key artifacts: Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/metering-overview?orgId=1, Kibana runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=87422
- Permanent fix: redesign aggregator checkpointing so the aggregator takes monotonic, idempotent checkpoints keyed by (producer, partition, window_end, checksum) and uses an append-only ledger to guard against replays.
- Private deployment changes: identify TTL cache paths that cause replay during backup/restore; replace with explicit dedupe store backed by RocksDB and a retention policy.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Stronger checkpointing and dedupe store will add storage overhead and slight read latency on write paths; however we prioritize correctness for billing.
- Locking windows reduces concurrency of aggregation so peak CPU may increase; mitigation is to shard windows by tenant for high-cardinality customers.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- No double-counted usage on a synthetic test plan of 7 days with induced restarts and replays.
- Rollout plan validated on staging and one Dedicated customer cluster.
- Automated end-to-end checks added to CI to detect hourly aggregation drift >0.5% vs raw logs.

Next steps & owners:
- Miguel Torres (owner): implement idempotent checkpointing and run load tests (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Priya Nambiar (SRE): add audit traces to aggregator and a Prometheus metric for 'duplicate_events_detected' (ETA 2026-03-14).
- Lena Fischer (Billing): finalize manual reconciliations and confirm crediting (ETA 2026-03-18).

Notes: Confluence postmortem template will be filled after RCA is completed and linked here. The team will coordinate a customer communication review with Legal/Support before any broad announcements.
